content:
We are pleased to introduce LeanHammer, an automated reasoning tool for Lean which combines multiple techniques for proof search and formal reconstruction. The hammer tactic searches for a proof of the current goal and then suggests a tactic script that can replace the hammer invocation. Example usage:

import Hammer
example (a b : Nat) : a + b = b + a := by
  hammer

You can also invoke our cloud-based neural premise selector only, using the premises tactic, which suggests relevant premises for the current goal.

LeanHammer currently works with versions of Mathlib based on Lean v4.20.0 as well as the current version of Mathlib. You can add LeanHammer to your project by inserting the following before requiring Mathlib:

[[require]]
name = "Hammer"
git = "https://github.com/JOSHCLUNE/LeanHammer"

You then need to execute lake update hammer. Additional information and instructions can be found in our repository.

LeanHammer builds on the work of many others. It relies on several independent projects and components, including:

  • Neural premise selection (repository, paper)
  • Symbolic premise selection using an implementation of the MePo filter due to Kim Morrison
  • Monomorphization and translation using Lean-auto (described here)
  • External automated theorem provers including Zipperposition and (in progress) cvc5
  • Native proof (re)construction using Aesop (described here) and Duper (described here), and (in progress) LeanSMT.

Technical details behind LeanHammer and its premise selection component can be found in our paper. LeanHammer is currently developed by @Thomas Zhu, @Josh Clune, @Jeremy Avigad, @Albert Jiang, and @Sean Welleck, with help from many people in the Lean Community.
